advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _snapshot_in_head treat only a git-confirmed 'object absent' (cat-file rc 1 against a resolvable HEAD) as False, and defer (return None) on other non-zero rcs (e.g. 128).
evidence: Docstring lines 114-117 acknowledge 'run_git_write(check=False) also fails non-zero on transient faults, and misreading one of those as "absent from HEAD" would revert a LANDED fold' yet only rc-124 is excluded from the False path.
run_git_write returns the verbatim non-zero rc after exhausting its retry budget (gitutil.py:554-560), so a persistent transient 128 reaches this branch as False.
advisory.finding: _snapshot_in_head only maps rc-124 to the INDETERMINATE (defer) result; any other non-zero, non-124 return from `git cat-file -e HEAD:<snapshot>` (e.g. a transient rc-128 'bad object'/FS fault that outlives run_git_write's retry budget) is read as a definite miss and returns False, causing recovery to REVERT a fold that may actually have committed — the exact 'revert a LANDED fold' hazard the docstring says it guards against.
advisory.suggested_fix: Return None for any probe rc that is neither 0 nor a definitive missing-object signal; e.g. treat only `probe.returncode == 1` as False and every other non-zero as indeterminate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Sanitize/validate ticket_id before using it as the journal filename (reject or encode path separators), or key the journal on a hash of the id.
evidence: pending_intents only lists names ending in '.json' (line 106); a ticket_id with a '/' would join into a subdir and not be discovered by listdir, so the journal would leak undetected.
advisory.finding: The intent journal filename is derived directly from the ticket id (f'{ticket_id}.json') with no sanitization; a ticket id containing a path separator or traversal component would place/lookup the journal outside the intent dir or collide, and write_intent/pending_intents/discard would silently disagree.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `_commit_backfill`/compact-all with compacted>0 and nothing left to stage still calls `push.push_after_commit` (spy that records the call, assert it fired).
evidence: compact.py:316-330 changed from `return` before push to falling through: `sys.stdout.write("No staged changes (the folds committed per ticket).\n")` ... `push.push_after_commit(tracker)`
docstring: 'The push must run even when nothing is staged, precisely BECAUSE the per-ticket commits are the ones waiting to be delivered.'
tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py:499 and :518 set `push_after_commit` to `lambda *a, **k: None` with no call assertion
test_a_sweep_that_folds_nothing_still_pushes (test_compact_all_selection.py:241) mocks compact_cli->0 so compacted==0 and routes through `_best_effort_push`, not `_commit_backfill`
dropped.finding: The behavioral change to `_commit_backfill` — removing the early `return` so the batched push runs even when nothing is staged (the stated purpose of the diff) — has no test asserting the push actually fires on the no-staged-changes path. Tests that reach `_commit_backfill` with committed folds (e.g. test_sweep_tree_is_committed_between_folds) monkeypatch `push_after_commit` to a bare no-op and never assert it was invoked; the existing `test_a_sweep_that_folds_nothing_still_pushes` covers the compacted==0 `_best_effort_push` path, not `_commit_backfill`'s branch.

evidence: tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py:139 `monkeypatch.setattr(_txn, "_retire_folded_sources", _boom)` where `_boom` raises RuntimeError — this hits the `except BaseException` path, not the `!= 0` return path

dropped.finding: The `_retire_folded_sources`-returns-nonzero branch of `_apply_fold` — which discards the intent journal and returns 1 WITHOUT calling `_abort_fold` (so recovery never reverts the intentionally-retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state) — is untested. The nearest test makes `_retire_folded_sources` raise, which exercises the `except BaseException`/`_abort_fold` path instead of the return-1 branch.
